The present claim petition has been filed by the petitioners against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-
with interest for the death of Sri. Puttaswami S/o. Eeregowda in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 28.12.2021.
SCCH-10 2

. The case of petitioners in brief is as under:
That, on 28.12.2021 at about 6.00 p.m., the deceased was proceeding in the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-11-X- 6127 as a pillion rider and the same was riding by its rider by name Praveen on K.M. Doddi - Mandya road.
When they reached near Madarahalli Lake, K.M.Doddi, Mandya District, the rider of said motor cycle ridden the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against a road side grill.
Due to the alleged accident, said Puttaswami fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to Government hospital, Mandya District.
After taking first aid, he was shifted to NIMHANS hospital and then to Victoria hospital where he died on 05.01.2022 at 11.15 a.m.
The petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the sons of the deceased and they are the legal heirs of deceased.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 58 years and he was doing agriculture and dairy farming and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.

Due to death of deceased, the petitioners have put to SCCH-10 mental shock and agony Padmamma vs Raju S.B on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87484807/
2 and also lost their bread earner of the family.

Further, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-11-X-6127.
As such, the respondent No.1 being owner and respondent No.2 being insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Hence,
the petitioners pray to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents under all heads together with interest and costs.
3. In response to the Petition notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed the written statement.

The respondent No.1 has not appeared before the Court,
remained absent and placed exparte.
4. The brief contentions of the respondent No.2 in the objection statement are as under:
The respondent No.2 contended that, the claim petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either SCCH-10 in law or on facts of the case.

The respondent has denied the accident, manner of accident and rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA- 11-X-6127 and also denied the age, occupation and income of the deceased.

Further, the respondent No.2 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle and in favour of the respondent No.1 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident, however the liability if any subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further, the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.

On these grounds,
respondent No.2 prayed for dismissal of the claim petition against it.
5. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed :

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that on 28.12.2022 at about 6.00 p.m., the deceased by name Puttaswamy was proceeding on Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-11-X-6127 as a pillion SCCH-10 rider and the same was ridden by its rider Praveen and when they reached near Madarahalli Lake, K.M. Doddi, Mandya, at that time, the rider of the said motor cycle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the road side grill.
Due to which the deceased fell down from the motor cycle and sustained grievous injury and succumbed to the said injuries ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the accident has mainly occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motor cycle ?
3) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased?
4) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed?

If so, at what rate and from whom?

My finding to the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.5
10. The petitioners have filed the present petition seeking compensation on the account of death of Sri. Puttaswami in a road traffic accident that occurred on 28-12-2021.

11. According to the petitioners, while deceased was proceeding in the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-11-X- 6127 as a pillion rider and the same was riding by its rider by name Praveen on K.M.
Doddi- Mandya road and the rider of said motor cycle ridden the same with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against a road side grill.

Further, due to the alleged accident, said Puttaswami SCCH-10 fell down and sustained grievous injuries and was shifted to Government hospital, Mandya District, later he was shifted to NIMHANS hospital and then to Victoria hospital where he died on 05.01.2022 at 11.15 a.m.
12.

To substantiate the said contentions, the petitioner No.2 got examined himself as PW-1 and got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15.
13.
Ex.P.1 is the FIR No.0297/2021 of K. M. Doddi PS and Ex.P.2 is the First information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, it reveal that, I.O. has registered a case against the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-11- X-6127 for the commission of offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.

Ex.P.7 is the charge sheet filed by the K.M. Doddi police against one Mr.
Praveen who is none other than the rider of the offending motor cycle.

Ex.P.5 and Ex.P.6 are the Padmamma vs Raju S.B on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87484807/
4
Inquest mahazar and Postmortem report respectively.
On perusal of postmortem report, it reveals that the deceased died due to coma as a result of SCCH-10 head injury sustained due to the accident.

On perusal of the aforesaid documents, it is sufficient to conclude that the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle and deceased succumbed to the injuries due to the accident.

14. Though the respondents have disputed the alleged accident and the manner of accident and also examined the rider of the motor cycle and the Investigation officer as RW-1 and RW-2 to substantiate their defence, the police records produced by the petitioners is sufficient to conclude that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle.
15. Besides, it is settled principles of law that in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.

In this view, Court receives support from the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachalapradesh Road SCCH-10 Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in the case of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.

Thus, by considering the present facts of the case and the materials placed on record, I am of the opinion that the accident in question had occurred due to the negligent and rash riding of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-11-X-6127 and the deceased Puttaswami succumbed to the injuries in the accident.
Hence, Issue No.1 & 2 are answered in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.3:-
It is the contention of the petitioners that, the petitioner No.1 is the wife, the petitioner No.2 and 3 are the sons of the deceased Puttaswami.
In order to prove the relationship with the deceased, the petitioners have produced copies of the Aadhaar cards as per Ex.P.8 to Ex.P.11 and PAN cards as per Ex.P.12 to Ex.P.14.
Ex.P.8 is the copy of Aadhaar card of the deceased.

Ex.P.9 is the copy of Aadhaar card of Smt.
Padamamma who is none other SCCH-10 than the wife of the deceased.
Ex.P.10 and Ex.P.11 are the Aadhaar cards of Manu.P and Naveen Kumkar. P (Petitioner No.2 and 3), who are the sons of the deceased.
The respondents have not much disputed the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.
On perusal of aforesaid documents, it disclose that the petitioners are the wife and sons of the deceased.

18. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 while canvassing his arguments has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in (2007) 10 Supreme Court Cases 643 in the case of Manjuri Bera (Smt) Vs Oriental Insurance company Ltd. & Another and judgment rendered by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2012 KAR 2859 in the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Reptd. By Sr. Divisional Manager, Vs David. T & Another and argued that the petitioner No.2 and 3 are the major sons and earning members and hence, they are not the dependents of the deceased and since the petitioner No.1 who is sole dependent, 50% shall be deducted towards SCCH-10 personal expenses.

Hon'ble Apex Court in the judgment reported in AIR 2020 SC 434 in the case of National Insurance company Ltd., Vs Birender & Others in para 15 it is held as under;
" It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

entities.text: National Insurance company Ltd., Vs Birender & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."
From the aforesaid dictum, it is clear that the earning son is also a legal representative and he is entitled compensation as a dependent.
20. In the instant case, the petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 and 3 are the sons of the deceased.
SCCH-10
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that the petitioner No.1 to 3 are the legal heirs and the dependents of the deceased.
Hence, I answer Issue No.3 in the Affirmative.
21. ISSUE No.4:

It is the specific contention of the petitioners that, deceased Puttaswami was hale and healthy at the time of accident and was an agriculturist and doing diary farming and earning a sum of Rs. 20,000/- per month.
It is further contended that, due to untimely death of deceased, the petitioners were put to great hardship and lost their bread earner of the family.
22. To prove the age of the deceased, the petitioners have produced copy of the Aadhaar card as per Ex.P.8, wherein, the date of birth of the deceased is shown as 01.01.1964.
The accident was occurred on 28.12.2021.
Therefore, at the time of accident, the deceased was aged 57 years.
23. Further, to prove the occupation and income of the SCCH-10 deceased, the petitioners have not produced any iota of documents.
Therefore, notional income has to be taken for consideration.
24. At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2023(4) KCCR 3603 (DB) between Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another.

entities.text: Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above decision the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru (KSLSA in short).

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The KSLSA, Bengaluru as per letter dated 26.02.2022 - 01/NLA/2022/550/2022 has circulated the notional income chart prepared by them.
As per the said notional income chart, if the accident occurred in the year 2021 the notional income has to be taken as Rs.15,000/- per month.

Therefore, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble High Court and the letter of KSLSA and also in the absence of proof of income, this Court is of the opinion that, if the notional income is taken into consideration for assessing the income of the deceased would be Padmamma vs Raju S.B on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87484807/
6 just and proper.
The SCCH-10 accident was occurred on 28-12-2021.
Therefore, this Court has taken Rs.15,000/- as monthly income of the deceased.

25. Before proceeding to award compensation under the different heads, I feel it necessary to reproduce the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in Special Leave Petition (Civil)
No.25590/2014 in between National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hon'ble Apex Court in para No.61 has proceeded to record the following conclusions;
(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case of the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the additions should be 15%.
(iv) In case the deceased was self- employed or on fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 SCCH-10 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component.

(v) For determination of the multiplicand, the deduction for personal and living expenses, the tribunals and the courts shall be guided by paragraphs 30 to 32 of Sarla Verma which we have reproduced hereinbefore.
(vi) The selection of multiplier shall be as indicated in the Table in Sarla Verma read with paragraph 42 of that judgment.
(vii) The age of the deceased should be the basis for applying the multiplier.
(viii) Reasonable figures on conventional head, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
26. As per the records, at the time of accident the deceased was aged 57 years.
Further, there is no dispute regarding the age of the deceased.
Hence, the age of the deceased is taken as 57 years at the time of accident for multiplier.

As per the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma SCCH-10 and Ors Vs. Delhi Transport Corp. and Anr reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 an operative multiplier of 9 is applicable for the age group of 56 to 60 years.

entities.text: Sarla Verma SCCH-10 and Ors Vs. Delhi Transport Corp. and Anr reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 27. In the instant case, the deceased left behind his wife and sons and they are dependents of the deceased.
In Sarla Verma case, the Hon'ble Apex Court has expressed the view regarding standardized deduction towards personal and living expenses.

Where the number of dependents are Padmamma vs Raju S.B on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87484807/
7 2 to 3, the deduction would be 1/3rd.

As discussed supra, in the present case, Petitioner No.1 (Wife),
Petitioner No.2 (son) and Petitioner No.3 (son) of the deceased are the dependents.
Hence, in the present case, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.
In the present case, the Court has taken the view that the deceased was having monthly income of Rs.15,000/- and annual income would be Rs.1,80,000/-.
If 1/3 rd is deducted towards personal expenses, the contribution to the family (dependents) is determined as Rs.1,20,000/-.
SCCH-10 28.

As per Pranay Sethi case, if the deceased was a self- employed or on fixed salary, an addition of 10% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was aged in between 56-60 years.
In the present case, the deceased was aged 57 years at the time of accident and was self employed.
Hence, an addition of 10% shall be added to Rs.1,20,000/-.
If an addition of 10% is added same will be (Rs.1,20,000/- + 10% (Rs.12,000/-) = Rs.1,32,000/-.
The multiplier will be 9 having regard to the age of the deceased at the time of death (57 years).
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.1,32,000/- X 9 = Rs.11,88,000/-.
Thus, Rs.11,88,000/- is the compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

29. As per Pranay Sethi Case, reasonable figures on conventional heads, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively.
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years from the SCCH-10 date of judgment (31.10.2017).

Therefore, in the instant case, the petitioners are entitled for the aforesaid conventional heads with enhanced rate of 20%.
30.

In Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and Ors., (Civil Appeal No.9581/2018), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held that the wife is entitled for spousal consortium and the children are entitled for parental consortium.

sentences.text: 31. As discussed above, since Loss of estate, Loss of Consortium and Funeral expenses has been fixed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi Case, the petitioners are entitled to receive Rs.18,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.48,000/-each (petitioner No.1 to 3) towards spousal and parental consortium and Rs.18,000/- towards funeral expenses.

32. The petitioners have contended that, immediately after the accident the injured was shifted to Government hospital, Mandya and after first aid, he was shifted to NIMHANS SCCH-10 hospital,
Bengaluru and later shifted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru and underwent and spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines and conveyance etc.
Ex.P.15 are the medical bills amounting to Rs.9,675/-.
The respondent No.2 has not seriously disputed the medical bills produced by the petitioners.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, a sum of Rs.9,675/- was spent towards medical expenses.
Therefore, petitioners are entitled for the actual medical bills of Rs.9,675/- and same is rounded off to Rs.9,700/-.

33. From the above discussions the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads:

REGARDING LIABILITY:

As discussed supra, this Court has arrived at the conclusion that, the accident had occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-11-X-6127.
The respondent No.1 has insured the vehicle with respondent No.2, as such, respondent No.2 has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Admittedly, the Insurance Policy was is in force at the time of the accident.
Therefore, the respondents No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award.

The respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation of Rs.13,77,700/- along with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization in the ratio of 50:25:25 respectively.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.4 Partly in the Affirmative.
SCCH-10 35. ISSUE No.5:

In view of my finding on Issue No.1 to 4, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.13,77,700/-with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
The petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled to receive compensation in the ratio of 50:25:25 respectively from the respondent No.2.

Out of the award amount, 50% of the award amount of petitioner No.1 to 3 shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank of petitioners' choice and balance amount shall be released to their SCCH-10 respective names through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- Draw award accordingly.

Though the respondents have disputed the alleged accident and the manner of accident and also examined the rider of the motor cycle and the Investigation officer as RW-1 and RW-2 to substantiate their defence, the police records produced by the petitioners is sufficient to conclude that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle.
15. Besides, it is settled principles of law that in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.
In this view, Court receives support from the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachalapradesh Road SCCH-10 Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in the case of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that the petitioner No.1 to 3 are the legal heirs and the dependents of the deceased.

The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 SCCH-10 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component.
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
Hence, the age of the deceased is taken as 57 years at the time of accident for multiplier.
As per the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma SCCH-10 and Ors Vs. Delhi Transport Corp. and Anr reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 an operative multiplier of 9 is applicable for the age group of 56 to 60 years.
Hence, in the present case, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.
In the present case, the Court has taken the view that the deceased was having monthly income of Rs.15,000/- and annual income would be Rs.1,80,000/-.
If 1/3 rd is deducted towards personal expenses, the contribution to the family (dependents) is determined as Rs.1,20,000/-.
As per Pranay Sethi case, if the deceased was a self- employed or on fixed salary, an addition of 10% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was aged in between 56-60 years.
In the present case, the deceased was aged 57 years at the time of accident and was self employed.
Hence, an addition of 10% shall be added to Rs.1,20,000/-.
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.1,32,000/- X 9 = Rs.11,88,000/-.
Thus, Rs.11,88,000/- is the compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
